qualification_scope: Bounded informational graph helpers only; no public replay-bundle acceptance or whole-system assurance claim.
authoring: Independently hand-authored before implementation; expected outputs are not generated by the proposed helper algorithms.
preserved_gates: All inherited source identity, contracts, proof, static analysis, tamper rejection, recovery, independent human validation, matched baseline, resource accounting, release and product acceptance gates remain binding. This contract changes none of them.

shared_semantics.representation: Post-decode JSON values. Exact Python built-in types only: dict, list, str, int, and NoneType as specified. bool and float never qualify as int, even when numerically integral. Tuples and subclasses are invalid.
shared_semantics.failure: Return exactly the error envelope; no nodes, order, partial result, warning-only continuation, or uncaught input-validation exception.
shared_semantics.output: Fresh JSON-compatible dict and list values; no input mutation. A successful result is deterministic for the declared input and contract version.
shared_semantics.parse_boundary: Raw JSON parsing, duplicate JSON object-member detection, encoding, depth and byte limits are upstream responsibilities and remain unqualified here. A decoded dict cannot recover discarded duplicate member names. These helpers must not be offered as a raw untrusted-byte parser.
shared_semantics.authority: Informational only. No hashing, authentication, identity, source membership, semantic truth, applicability, freshness, currentness, quorum agreement or authorization conclusion follows.
shared_semantics.baseline: Use these same helpers and limits over both the original-source baseline graph and the transport-derived graph. No representation receives a privileged checker.
shared_semantics.resources: Inputs admitted to graph processing contain at most 32 nodes, 64 edges and 32 changed indices; predecessor processing contains at most 8 entries. Validate outer types and collection limits before traversing contents. Reject excess inputs, never truncate. All processing loops and auxiliary storage must have explicit bounds derived from these constants; no recursion. Service loops are not part of these helpers.

input.edges: exact list of at most 64 exact lists [dependent_index,required_index]
input.changed_nodes: exact list of at most 32 unique exact int indices

reverse_reachable.direction: [d,r] states that d depends on r. A change to r affects d. A change to d does not, solely through this edge, affect r.
reverse_reachable.index_universe: All indices are exact ints satisfying 0 <= index < node_count. Every such index declares one graph node, including isolated nodes. No separate labels or implicit nodes exist.
reverse_reachable.duplicates: Duplicate directed edge pairs and duplicate changed indices are errors; reversed edge pairs are distinct but together form a cycle.
reverse_reachable.acyclicity: The entire graph must be acyclic, including components unreachable from changed_nodes. A self-edge is a cycle. Check this even when changed_nodes is empty.
reverse_reachable.meaning: Return the least set S containing all changed_nodes such that for every declared edge [d,r], membership of r in S implies membership of d in S. Include seeds even when isolated. Sort resulting node indices in increasing numeric order.
validation_precedence: G_MISSING_FIELD if any required field is absent
G_UNKNOWN_FIELD if any field outside closed_fields is present
G_SCHEMA unless type(schema) is str and value is exactly quorum/graph-development/1

For each edge in input order: G_EDGE_SHAPE unless type(edge) is list and length is 2; then for dependent followed by required, G_INDEX_TYPE unless type(index) is int, else G_INDEX_RANGE unless in declared universe; then G_DUPLICATE_EDGE if this exact pair occurred earlier
For each changed index in input order: G_INDEX_TYPE unless type(index) is int; then G_INDEX_RANGE unless in declared universe; then G_DUPLICATE_CHANGED if the same index occurred earlier
G_CYCLE if any directed cycle exists anywhere in the declared graph
Otherwise return exactly status=ok and nodes as defined above

predecessor_order.input: Exact list containing at most 8 entries. Entry i is None (JSON null) for a root, or an exact int index of the update that must precede i. The literal string root is invalid. There is no wrapper schema for this internal helper.
predecessor_order.index_universe: One update exists for every array position, including roots. All predecessor references must be in [0,len(predecessors)). A later array position may be a predecessor of an earlier one.
predecessor_order.meaning: Return every update index once. A referenced predecessor must occur before its dependent. At each position select the smallest numeric index among all not-yet-emitted updates whose predecessor is null or has already been emitted. This is the lexicographically smallest valid topological order.
predecessor_order.cycles: Reject every self-reference and directed cycle anywhere, including a cycle disconnected from roots. Never return a partial order.
validation_precedence: For each entry in input order: null is valid; otherwise P_INDEX_TYPE unless type(entry) is int, then P_INDEX_RANGE unless in declared universe
P_CYCLE for any self-reference or longer cycle
Otherwise return exactly status=ok and order as defined above

oracle_use.expectations: Each case contains one literal call input and one exact literal expected output. Do not compute expected output by calling helpers, copying helper intermediate state or implementing the same graph algorithm in an oracle generator.
oracle_use.coverage_limits: Finite component examples are not exhaustive proof, semantic adjudication, replay qualification, recovery evidence or a heldout/external campaign. They do not prove arbitrary language semantics or completeness of declared dependencies.
oracle_use.smallest_next_step: Sole owner freezes file identities and obtains actual GPT-6.1 independent review before implementation, then implements only these bounded helpers and executes the frozen examples with original controls retained.
oracle_use.acceptance_evidence: Exact source identity, unchanged frozen oracle and contract digests, actual GPT-6.1 review disposition, bounded implementation inspection, strict applicable analysis, full literal-case results with failures retained, input nonmutation checks and identical helper use in both development comparison arms. Whole-system and external gates remain additional requirements.
